chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) who shaved his head in Mecca. He said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did that in the first thirty days of the months of Hajj, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did it after the thirty days in which hair is allowed to grow for Hajj, then there is upon him a dam (blood offering) which he must pour out.' And whenever one forgets the Taqsir (partial shaving/cutting) until he enters the state of Ihram for Hajj, a dam becomes obligatory upon him; this was narrated.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and the first ten days of Muharram)
key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: Entered the state of Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرَ: Partial shaving or cutting of hair (the initial act of exiting Umrah Ihram)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah and then Hajj in the same season
key_terms.يُوفَّرُ فِيهَا الشَّعْرُ: In which hair is allowed to grow (to a specific length)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for shaving the head early during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the penalty for premature shaving in Hajj al-Tamattu' depends on intent and timing: ignorance incurs no penalty, while deliberate action after the hair has grown sufficiently (approximately 30 days into Dhul-Hijjah) requires a blood offering (dam). This distinction highlights the juristic principle of balancing ritual precision with practical ease for the pilgrim.
